key_insight: An integrated deep learning and adaptive control method aims to adjust robotic GMAW planning and welding parameters as joint conditions change.
engineering_relevance: The approach targets reduced manual reprogramming and more consistent weld formation despite machining errors, assembly deviations and thermal effects.
method: Combine quality-grade-oriented process planning with site-specific multi-objective parameter optimization.
Use semi-supervised seam and molten-pool segmentation with neural-network weld-formation prediction.
Apply fuzzy adaptive control to respond to changing welding conditions.
evidence_signal: Experiments used Q235 steel butt joints, with a response surface model linking current, welding speed, torch angle and nozzle height to weld geometry; the abstract reports no quantitative performance gains.
watch_item: Generalization beyond Q235 butt joints and real-time robustness under shop-floor conditions remain unestablished in the abstract.
paper_title: Deep Learning-Based Welding Process Optimization and Adaptive Control Method for Welding Robots
